speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; to begin my assessment, please describe your specific symptoms in detail and tell me about any past diagnoses or surgeries you have had.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, Vitamin_B12_level, Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone, Syphilis_Serology.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial workup for common metabolic and infectious causes of ataxia appears normal. Can you tell me specifically when your ataxia symptoms began, and have you noticed any numbness, weakness, or balance issues that are worse in the dark? Additionally, do you have any history of alcohol use disorder or diabetes?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your description of clumsiness predominantly on the right side and a recent onset, please specify exactly which limb movements are affected (e.g., finger-to-nose, heel-to-shin) and whether you experience any involuntary tremors or jerking movements. Additionally, do you have a known history of multiple sclerosis, cervical spine issues, or any recent head trauma?

REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain, Cervical_Spine_MRI, Cerebrospinal_Flux.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. Cervical_Spine_MRI: NORMAL READINGS. Cerebrospinal_Flux: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions in the brain without enhancement are pathognomonic for PML, likely secondary to an undiagnosed or suppressed immune system (e.g., HIV or chemotherapy). I recommend immediate testing for HIV and immunosuppressive agents.
